paper_title: RLPlanner: Reinforcement Learning based Floorplanning for Chiplets with Fast Thermal Analysis

scenario.figure_or_table: Table I (Ascend 910 System column); pinned config/Ascend910.cfg
scenario.description: Ascend 910 System benchmark (ref [6]) from RLPlanner. The pinned config lists 6 chiplets with widths (mm) 14.5, 10.5, 7.75, 7.75, 7.75, 7.75, heights (mm) 31.4, 16, 11.87 x4, and powers (W) 256, 14, 20, 20, 20, 20. No final placement coordinates or power time series are published in the packet. Table I reports Ascend 910 results of reward -7.4063, wirelength 18130 mm, maximum temperature 77.12 C, runtime 7773 s for RLPlanner.
scenario.architecture: 2.5D chiplet-based system with 6 chiplets (Ascend 910) on an interposer; floorplanned by RLPlanner (PPO RL agent with RND bonus)
scenario.workload: Static per-chiplet power values from the pinned Ascend910.cfg; no time-varying workload published
scenario.operating_point: Steady-state maximum temperature as the thermal observable, reported in C in Table I (RLPlanner 77.12 C); the temperature limit T0 is not stated in the packet

original_setup.solver: HotSpot (open-source compact thermal solver) is the ground-truth reference; RLPlanner uses its own physics-informed fast thermal model, an LTI self/mutual thermal resistance network characterized from HotSpot runs (2D self-thermal table plus 1D mutual-thermal table). It reports 0.2523 K MAE against HotSpot and a 127x speed-up (PDF p.2, Table II).
original_setup.optimizer: RLPlanner: PPO-trained policy/value networks with a shared CNN encoder and a random network distillation (RND) exploration bonus. Chiplets are placed sequentially with an action mask, and microbump assignment is done before thermal evaluation. Baselines are TAP-2.5D (simulated annealing) with HotSpot or with the fast thermal model (PDF p.1-2).
original_setup.controller: None. This is early-stage static floorplanning with no runtime thermal controller or DTM. The RL agent is a placement optimizer, not a thermal controller.
original_setup.benchmark: Ascend 910 System (ref [6], PDF p.2 Table I): 6 chiplets, with the pinned config/Ascend910.cfg giving widths, heights and powers. Reported RLPlanner result: reward -7.4063, wirelength 18130 mm, max temperature 77.12 C, runtime 7773 s. The paper does not state which RLPlanner variant (RND or non-RND) the 77.12 C row is, beyond the row label RLPlanner.

thermal_observable.location: Maximum operating temperature of the chiplet system (Ascend 910 System, RLPlanner row), evaluated after floorplanning and microbump assignment. The exact spatial location is not specified.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum temperature over the system (steady-state), reported as a single value per method in Table I. The paper does not specify the number of runs or whether this is a mean or best over runs.

physical_mismatches.reason: Studio models a simple 2D steady-state placement. The paper's HotSpot and fast thermal model describe a 2.5D chiplet-on-interposer stack with package layers, and the packet gives no interposer, TIM, heat spreader or heat sink parameters. A 2D representation omits vertical stack and interposer lateral spreading effects.

Cooling and boundary conditions (heat sink, convection, ambient temperature) are not published in the packet. The paper's 77.12 C therefore cannot be reproduced or numerically compared to Studio results.

The final RLPlanner placement coordinates for the Ascend 910 are not published, so x_m and y_m of each chiplet are unknown. Any Studio placement would be a separate illustrative layout, not the paper's floorplan.

The paper's temperature comes from RL-optimized placement co-optimized with wirelength and a temperature-limit reward. The fast thermal model has about 0.25 K MAE relative to HotSpot, and it is unclear which solver produced the Table I temperatures. Studio's solver differs from both.

The paper has no transient behavior or time-series power. The one-row static power trace is consistent with the steady-state paper observable, but there is no controller or reliability analysis to compare.
Final chiplet coordinates are not supplied by the reference files; generated shelf positions illustrate a 2D power snapshot, not the published placement.

studio_assumptions: Any Studio run would use a separately constructed illustrative 2D placement, with generated coordinates kept distinct from paper-derived facts.
Powers would be a one-row static trace from the pinned Ascend910.cfg: 256, 14, 20, 20, 20, 20 W.

Chiplet dimensions would come from the pinned config, converted from mm to m (conversion factor 0.001): widths 14.5, 10.5, 7.75, 7.75, 7.75, 7.75 mm and heights 31.4, 16, 11.87, 11.87, 11.87, 11.87 mm.

Chiplet names are not given in the config, so generic indexed names would be used, with the order assumed to match the config lists. Which chiplet is the 256 W compute die is inferred from the largest power and size, not stated.
Studio's own package, material and cooling assumptions apply and are not specified in the packet. Studio temperatures are not numerically compared to the paper's 77.12 C.
RLPlanner publishes Ascend910 chiplet sizes and powers, but this config has no placement, power time series, or HotSpot configuration.
The power trace is one constant row made from source per-chiplet watts.
